key_idea: Find the streets that have only 2 houses. The new house must be on both of them.
steps: The top street has only 2 houses. The middle and bottom streets already have 3 each.
The circle on the right has only 2 houses: the one in the middle of the middle street and the one at the bottom right.
Point A is on the top street and on the right circle, so one house there fixes both.

choice_feedback.B: B is on the top street, but not on the right circle.
choice_feedback.C: C is on the middle street, which already has 3 houses.
choice_feedback.D: D is not on the top street, and not on the right circle.
choice_feedback.E: E is on the bottom street, which already has 3 houses.

review.note: The circles are drawn as filled discs that cover each other, so parts of the left and middle circles are hidden: the left circle's arc through the centre house at (280,200), where it touches the right circle, and the middle circle's arc through the house at (420,200) cannot be seen. A child counting visible houses finds only 2 on the left and middle circles. Key A checks out by geometry and the steps only use the top street and the fully visible right circle; redraw the circles unfilled.
